## 6. Decision rule applied verbatim

1. `INVALID_ATTEMPT`: a common-integrity failure, nonfinite required observable, learner-side
   instrumentation failure, or nonzero-count mismatch. Quarantine; no scientific polarity.
2. `B9R1_RECEIVER_ADDRESSED_SEMANTIC_EDGE`: `J > 0` and `Delta_R > 0` in the global, both-anchor,
   every leave-one-profile and every leave-one-root aggregate, while global
   `receiver_correct_vs_anchor >= 0` and `receiver_correct_vs_source >= 0`.
3. `B9R1_GENERIC_OR_SOURCE_HARM_ONLY`: the semantic branch fails and at least one holds: global
   generic gain is positive; global source-vs-anchor, receiver-vs-anchor, or receiver-vs-source
   CORRECT difference is negative; or any robustness aggregate has `Delta_R <= 0`.
4. `B9R1_RECEIVER_NOT_SUPPORTED`: branches 1--3 fail and `J <= 0` for both anchor means.
5. `B9R1_MIXED_UNIDENTIFIED`: every remaining valid complete result.

Branch 1 does not apply: integrity, finite observables, instrumentation, and counts all pass.
Branch 2 fails because global and A0 `Delta_R` are negative, A0 `J` is negative, every
leave-one-profile/root `Delta_R` is negative, and both global CORRECT comparisons required to be
nonnegative are negative. Branch 3 then applies independently through negative global
source-vs-anchor, receiver-vs-anchor, and receiver-vs-source CORRECT differences and through every
robust `Delta_R <= 0`. Generic gain itself is negative; it is not the trigger.

## 7. Bounded reading

Direct observation: this immediate one-step receiver-addressed update did not produce the frozen
robust semantic edge. A1 has positive receiver-versus-source `J` and positive `Delta_R`, but both
receiver- and source-addressed CORRECT rewards are below the unchanged A1 anchor. A0 has negative
`J` and `Delta_R`; the global and every leave-one robustness `Delta_R` are negative.

Strongest support for a receiver-relative effect is A1 (`J=0.0006159866`,
`Delta_R=0.0000314092`). Strongest contradiction is the A0 reversal plus the negative global
absolute CORRECT effects and uniformly negative leave-one `Delta_R`. The surviving explanation is
strong initialization sensitivity and/or a one-step displacement too small or misaligned for the
native evaluator.

This result does not establish a general negative, receiver-local mediation, stable or sustained
learning, superiority of source addressing, generic credit-assignment harm, CBSC static-content
polarity, transfer, safety, lifecycle, priority, or C readiness. It closes only this B/EXPLORE
one-step object; B objects have no consumption state.
